errors.english: how does a cognition arise from a word and the like that is not the exclusion of others, when exclusion as the meaning of words has been refuted?
errors.why: The Tibetan asks how, from words that are not exclusion, a cognition arises with respect to (ལ) the negation of exclusion as word-meaning, i.e. the negation is the content of that cognition (cf. previous side), not a prior circumstance.

note: A careful rendering of Kamalaśīla's apoha discussion; only the opponent's question at the side's middle is slightly misconstrued.

errors.english: It is incorrect for space [note: original: (nam mkha'); space or ether] to possess a nature [note: original: (rang bzhin); inherent nature or essence] because it is logical that the essence of one distinct entity is separate from another distinct entity.
errors.why: The Tibetan says the qualities (pervasiveness etc.) cannot be the nature of space, because it is NOT reasonable for the nature of one thing to be a different, separate thing.

fix.find: It is incorrect for space [note: original: (nam mkha'); space or ether] to possess a nature [note: original: (rang bzhin); inherent nature or essence] because it is logical that the essence of one distinct entity is separate from another distinct entity.
fix.replace: [Those qualities] cannot be the nature [note: original: (rang bzhin); inherent nature or essence] of space [note: original: (nam mkha'); space or ether], because it is not reasonable for the nature of one entity to be a different, separate entity.

errors.english: Likewise, it is impossible for them to possess number, because those two [note: referring to number and collection] are themselves types of qualities
errors.why: གྲངས་དང་ལྡན་པ are the two Vaiśeṣika qualities number (saṃkhyā) and conjunction (saṃyoga), which reside only in substances; it is not 'possessing number', and 'collection' is not a guṇa.

fix.find: Likewise, it is impossible for them to possess number, because those two [note: referring to number and collection] are themselves types of qualities
fix.replace: Likewise, number and conjunction are also impossible [for them], because those two [note: number (saṃkhyā) and conjunction (saṃyoga)] are themselves types of qualities

errors.english: Similarly, there are no distinctions among the collection of the six categories
errors.why: The Tibetan applies the same challenge to the expression 'the collection of the six categories': one should ask, if there is no difference, how are they six? It does not assert that there are no distinctions.

note: The Vaiśeṣika argument is mostly followed, but the opening reason is inverted and number/conjunction is mistranslated and mis-glossed.

errors.english: although the object of sound does not have a nature of various conjunctions
errors.why: སྒྲ here is the word ('variegated'): the point is that a variegated conjunction is not the referent of that word, not 'the object of sound'.

errors.english: the metaphor exists because of the "inherence" [note: original: "samavaya"] of many things into a single object of conjunction
errors.why: The Tibetan says the conjunction inheres in a single object (ekārthasamavāya), not that many things inhere in a single object of conjunction.

note: The anti-avayavin argument about variegated colour is rendered faithfully on the whole, with two technical constructions blurred.

errors.english: (Upali) The Buddha's disciple foremost in knowledge of Vinaya or monastic discipline replied, "It should be given."
errors.why: ཉེ་བ་འཁོར is a vocative: Upāli asks the question and the Buddha answers 'Upāli, it should be given'; the English makes Upāli the one who replies.

fix.find: (Upali) The Buddha's disciple foremost in knowledge of Vinaya or monastic discipline replied, "It should be given."
fix.replace: The Buddha replied, "Upāli, it should be given."

errors.english: The intention is that such a son will not return to being the master of the father's house.
errors.why: The Tibetan gives the reason one may accept from the expelled son: he does not cease to be an owner of the father's household.

fix.find: The intention is that such a son will not return to being the master of the father's house.
fix.replace: The intention is that such a son does not cease to be an owner of the father's household.

errors.english: if the robes are not being worn and are thus separated from the person
errors.why: Here བགོ means divide/distribute: if the goods are not divided they are no longer held jointly, so what is given to the distributor counts as properly given; it is not about wearing robes.

errors.english: [note: referring to property associated with the deceased or the transition of inheritance]
errors.why: The rule concerns a person turned back from the charnel ground (a cemetery-dweller, as the next side discusses), not inheritance of the deceased's property.

note: Vinaya distribution rules are muddled: the Upāli exchange is misassigned, the expelled-son rule inverted, and inline glosses intrude into the text.

errors.english: the prince, together with the chief ministers, approached the lord of beings.
errors.why: The subjects (སྐྱེ་རྒུ, prajāḥ), together with the prince and chief ministers, went to their lord; the people as agents are dropped.

note: A good verse rendering of the Kalpalatā lament; only the subject of the first stanza is narrowed.

errors.english: Therefore, positive concomitance requires that the presence of the reason is pervaded by the presence of the probandum [note: Tibetan: བསྒྲུབ་བྱ་, Sanskrit: sādhya] in all cases. Alternatively, the negative concomitance
errors.why: The negation governs both members: neither anvaya (pervasion in all cases) nor vyatireka is established by merely seeing probandum and reason together in some instances; the English turns the first into a free-standing requirement.

errors.english: there must be a valid cognition [note: Tibetan: ཚད་མ་, Sanskrit: pramāṇa] that establishes the relation between the explained concordant class and the non-concordant class.
errors.why: The Tibetan says that only when there is a pramāṇa establishing the (reason–probandum) relation are presence and absence in the sapakṣa and vipakṣa as described established; the relation is not between the two classes.

note: Terminology (sapakṣa, vipakṣa, anvaya, vyatireka) is right, but the argument about why mere observation does not yield concomitance is restructured in two places.

errors.english: Through the pride of the lord of men [note: original Sanskrit: "na vi mā nena", referring to a king], the lotus of his face lost its beauty.
errors.why: མ་བཀུར་པ་དེས (Skt. vimānena) is 'through that disrespect' (the insult the king suffered, from the previous side), not the king's pride; the note mis-segments the Sanskrit.

fix.find: Through the pride of the lord of men [note: original Sanskrit: "na vi mā nena", referring to a king], the lotus of his face lost its beauty.
fix.replace: Through that disrespect [note: Tibetan ma bkur pa, Sanskrit vimāna], the lotus of the lord of men's face lost its beauty.

note: The verses are rendered well apart from the opening, where the king's humiliation becomes his pride.
A faithful rendering of the defence of the Mahāyāna as Buddha-word, with the patriarchal lineage correctly named.

errors.english: [note: referring to a ritual source of fire or a specific lightning-fire]
errors.why: In Dharmakīrti's verse śakramūrdhan ('Indra's head') is the anthill, from which a smoke-like vapour rises; it is not a ritual fire or lightning.

fix.find: [note: referring to a ritual source of fire or a specific lightning-fire]
fix.replace: [note: Sanskrit śakramūrdhan, a name for an anthill, from which a smoke-like vapour rises]

errors.english: heavy clay
errors.why: ལྕི་བ here is cow dung (gomaya), the standard example of a dissimilar cause, not 'heavy clay'.

errors.english: Otherwise, there would be no purpose [note: or occurrence] at any time.
errors.why: ལན་འགའ means 'occasional' (kādācitka): otherwise there would be no occasional occurrence of anything; it is not about purpose.

errors.english: for the sake of determining the specific place and time
errors.why: ཕྱིར is causal here: because [smoke] is restricted to a particular place and time, its being seen and not seen shows its nature of being produced by that cause.

note: The causal argument is broadly intelligible, but a famous example is mis-glossed and a standard term is mistranslated.

errors.english: these phenomena are neither unafflicted nor are they afflicted
errors.why: The sūtra says these phenomena are without affliction and are not afflicted; 'neither unafflicted' adds a negation.

fix.find: these phenomena are neither unafflicted nor are they afflicted
fix.replace: these phenomena are free of affliction; they are not afflicted

errors.english: Recognizing the origination of all phenomena
errors.why: In this Akṣayamatinirdeśa passage འབྱུང་བ is emergence/deliverance (niryāṇa), as in the preceding 'in which there is no emergence': knowing all phenomena as leading to deliverance, not their origination.

note: A sound rendering of Prajñākaramati's sūtra citation, with one inverted line and an ambiguous term taken in the wrong sense.
